statement: Compute zone and space heating and cooling loads from the analytical energy model, climate and internal gains.

source.ref: About Heating and Cooling Loads Analysis

superiority: Run loads locally in seconds and show per-surface contribution breakdown.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Load for a single-zone box matches a reference steady-state calculation within 5 percent.

statement: Create an energy analytical model and run cloud-based energy simulation for design alternatives.
superiority: Run simulation locally with transparent assumptions and no cloud wait.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Analytical model surface areas match physical areas within 0.5 percent.

statement: Configure how the energy model is generated: mode (masses and building elements, rooms or spaces), phase, ground plane, analytical space and surface resolution, perimeter zones, building type and the source of thermal properties.
superiority: Show each default used in the analysis with its source value.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Location is set with a separate Location tool, not in Energy Settings. Acceptance sketch: Changing building type changes the default schedules used in analysis.

statement: Generate the energy model's analytical spaces, each a discrete volume of air, from rooms, spaces or masses and building elements, and review them in a dedicated 3D view and schedule.

source.ref: About Spaces in the Energy Model

superiority: Detect and fix bad gaps between spaces automatically.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: 'Boundary conditions' is a structural term; energy spaces are volumes generated from rooms/spaces/masses. Acceptance sketch: Space volume equals the room volume within 0.1 percent.

statement: Build analytical surfaces as the heat-transfer boundaries between spaces and the outdoors, each with adjacency, surface type (such as exterior wall, roof, shade or air) and planar or rectangular geometry.

source.ref: About Surfaces in the Energy Model

superiority: Edit surface types in bulk with preview.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Original page candidates were the structural analytical model; the energy surfaces topic is this one. Acceptance sketch: Surface area and normal match the source face.

statement: Give each window or door opening in the energy model its own analytical surface that references its parent surface and originating architectural element.
superiority: Detect and heal missing or duplicated openings automatically before analysis.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: The structural 'Analytical Openings' page is a different feature; area/type of energy openings is not detailed in help. Acceptance sketch: Opening area equals the glazing area of each window within 0.5 percent.

statement: Export the energy analytical model as gbXML for external analysis.

source.ref: Export to gbXML Using Energy Settings

superiority: Round trip results back as an overlay.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Exported gbXML space count equals the model.

statement: Run a solar study from view settings that shows shadow positions for date and time ranges.
superiority: Animate and export a day sweep with a time slider.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Shadow length at noon equals height over tan(altitude).

statement: Show the sun path diagram with date, time and project location in views.
superiority: Make sun path adjustments through a live timeline.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Sun position at a given time matches an astronomical algorithm within 0.1 degrees.

statement: Evaluate daylight potential in a room or on a floor plane with simulation.
superiority: Fast preview with progressive results.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Daylight factor in a reference box matches closed form within 10 percent.

statement: Display analysis results as color surfaces, diagrams or vectors with legends and ranges.
superiority: Interactive probing of values at any point.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Legend range matches the min/max of the results.

statement: Add custom analysis results to a view through a framework with display styles.

source.ref: Display Styles for Analysis Add-In Applications

superiority: Standard open interface for analysis plug-ins.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Custom result values show on the surface in the legend.

statement: Compute the shortest route between a start and end point on a single level in a plan view, steering around obstacle elements, as a view-specific element that can be tagged and scheduled.
superiority: Account for stairs, doors and widths for egress checks.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page states path of travel is calculated on one level and ignores stairs and ramps; 'across levels' is wrong. Acceptance sketch: Route length between two points in a corridor equals the straight line plus corner detours.

statement: Check duct systems and mark in the view those that are not assigned to a user-defined system, are not connected as one network, or have flow, demand or flow-direction mismatches.
superiority: Provide a one-click fix suggestion for each issue type.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Size issues are not part of the check. Acceptance sketch: Check reports a deliberately broken run and passes the intact run.

statement: Check electrical circuits to verify each is properly connected to a panel, listing errors with a Show option that highlights the offending device.
superiority: Suggest a balanced assignment of devices across circuits.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Overloaded circuits are not part of this check (a rating warning exists elsewhere in circuit properties). Acceptance sketch: A circuit above its panel rating is flagged.

statement: Report duct pressure loss per path with per-section and fitting breakdown.
superiority: Export the report to a spreadsheet with the formulas visible.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Straight-duct loss equals the Darcy-Weisbach closed form within 2 percent.

statement: Report pipe pressure loss per path with section breakdown including fittings.
superiority: Cite the friction model used and export the table to a spreadsheet.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Straight-run loss equals the Darcy-Weisbach closed form within 2 percent.

statement: Use panel schedules to show each panel, its circuits and a loads summary, with demand factors driving demand loads; connected and demand load reporting is per panel and circuit.
superiority: Update continuously as devices change and export to a standard sheet.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: No dedicated electrical analysis report or voltage-drop report found; loads appear in panel schedules and circuit properties. Acceptance sketch: Report totals equal the sum of circuit loads.

statement: Exchange the structural model with an external structural analysis program in both directions, bring back static analysis results and required reinforcement, and review results as overlays through a Results Explorer.
superiority: Use an open exchange format so any analysis tool can be linked.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Documented as Robot Structural Analysis integration plus Results Explorer; generic 'strength checks' are not described. Acceptance sketch: Check results appear for each member in the sample frame.

statement: List all current model warnings in a reviewable list, and for a selected element list its related warnings with the involved elements highlighted in views.
superiority: Group, prioritise and auto-fix warnings with batch resolution.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Review Warnings is a Manage > Inquiry tool; related-element warnings are a Modify tab tool. Duplicate-mark examples not verified. Acceptance sketch: Warning list count matches known conditions in a test file.

statement: Display all constraints in a view with temporary visibility to understand dependencies.
superiority: Always show a persistent dependency overlay for selected element.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Constraints shown for a locked element.

statement: Materials can carry a carbon asset with a carbon database, a carbon category and an embodied-carbon coefficient, shown with an indicator on materials that have one so they can be filtered.
superiority: Open emission factor data with provenance and region per material.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: 'Used in schedules and analysis' is not stated on the page; library materials come pre-mapped to categories. Acceptance sketch: Carbon total equals volume times density times factor for a sample wall.

statement: A cloud carbon analysis reports a building's embodied carbon in a detail dashboard where embodied-carbon definitions for materials and products can be viewed and edited.
superiority: Update live as design changes and compare options.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Per-assembly/material/level breakdown could not be verified: the Embodied Carbon Details page itself could not be fetched. Acceptance sketch: Report total equals the sum of element carbon.

statement: Compute room areas and volumes with configurable computation settings and expose them in properties, tags and schedules.
superiority: Reconcile area scheme totals automatically and highlight differences.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Documented for rooms (spaces have a sibling topic); no report by level/scheme is described. Acceptance sketch: Report totals equal the sum of the element values per level.

statement: Measure distance between two points or along an element.
superiority: Persistent measurement annotations.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Measured length equals analytic distance.

statement: Produce an interference report listing conflicting element pairs for coordination review.
superiority: Group clashes by cause and assign them to people with status.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Report lists exactly the known overlapping pairs in a seeded test model.

statement: Check piping systems and mark in the view those not assigned to a user-defined system, not connected as one network, or with flow, demand or flow-direction mismatches.
superiority: Offer one-click fix suggestions for each flagged item.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page lists flow/demand configuration and flow direction mismatches rather than 'flow classification errors'. Acceptance sketch: Check reports a deliberately broken pipe run and passes a clean one.

statement: Evaluate solar radiation on surfaces over a time range and display it as a colour overlay.
superiority: Provide hourly radiation maps from open climate data inside the model.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Radiation on a horizontal surface matches reference tables within 10 percent.

statement: Compute illuminance on a work plane with electric and daylight sources and show the result.
superiority: Run progressive local results with no upload.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Illuminance under a point source matches the inverse-square law within 5 percent.
